single_turn_and_controlled_family: All excited-state coefficients in N are negative, so Nprime>0. N(1)=0 then gives strict overlap signs on both sides, including beta=0.
Expanded Nprime Z-N Zprime into (w_i-w_j)(E_j-E_i)exp(-beta(E_i+E_j)); checked all six signs and c13>c23.
Regrouped J=exp(beta E4)D exactly. E4>E2+E3 makes the exponents positive; c13>c23 makes the inner factor positive. Every nonconstant summand strictly increases.
J(1)>0 follows from Nprime(1)Z(1)>0. J(0)<0 gives exactly one root in (0,1); J(0)>=0 gives none for beta>0, including equality.
Since b<0 on cooling, the unique derivative sign change is a magnitude maximum. Two positive beta values before it give finite preparations; no infinite-temperature witness is required.
On heating beta>1, J and b are positive, so the overlap magnitude has ordinary ordering.
Checked exact family bath orthogonality, conservation, detailed balance, and all four eigenvector equations. First equation gives lambda; second and fourth determine the varying rates.
Reviewed Bernstein conversion on z=lo+(hi-lo)t: coefficient k is sum_j<=k power_j binomial(k,j)/binomial(n,j). Positive coefficients and positive denominators certify every point of the interval.
Reviewed continuous checks of both varying-rate bounds, all eight strict F/G margins, branch signs, eigenvalue interval and mode hypotheses; rational inequalities do not accept floating samples.
Baseline symmetric form diag(q)(M0 transpose+50I) has nonzero LDL pivots with signs +,-,+,-. Congruence inertia gives exactly two eigenvalues below -50.

Increasing reversible rates increases the nonnegative Dirichlet form. Min-max preserves two eigenvalues below -50. Explicit lambda lies in (-20,-19); zero is simple by positivity. Four eigenvalues are exhausted, so the constructed mode is simple and slowest.
Second spectral check uses trace and trace-square to determine the residual quadratic. Reversibility gives real roots; positive value at -50 and mean below -50 place both below -50.
Substituting r=r0+eta z gives D0=U-Vz. Rational log enclosures establish V>0 and the strict printed bracket for U/V.
Log implementation reduces arguments to [1,2], uses t=(a-1)/(a+1) and the positive series; its remainder is at most 2t^(2m+1)/((2m+1)(1-t^2)). Checked endpoints and rounding direction.
Fixed-pair overlaps have affine form u+zv and are both negative. Positive v_h-v_c makes reversal equivalent to z>-(u_h-u_c)/(v_h-v_c). Integer-power bisection encloses each rational power.

At onset Jprime>0 and D=0 imply d*>0. D0=-V delta and Z0=4 give bprime(0)=-V delta/16 and bdoubleprime(0,z*)=d*/16. Taylor expansion gives beta_m=V delta/d*+O(delta^2) and magnitude gain V^2 delta^2/(32d*)+O(delta^3).
ordered_conductance_theorem: G_ijk=q_j(k_ik-k_jk), with q_j positive, establishes exact equivalence to ordered reduced conductances.
Every prefix contrast has q-mean zero. Its product with a longer contrast sums to zero; norm squared is Q_k Q_(k+1)/q_(k+1). The n-1 nonzero orthogonal vectors span the mean-zero space.
Detailed balance makes normalized contrast generator A symmetric. Derived Lh_l for i<=k+1<=l, then subtracted the k+1 value to obtain the printed off-diagonal identity with nonnegative differences.
Shifting A by cI makes every entry nonnegative. The exponential series then proves exp(tA)>=0 with strictly positive diagonal at finite t>=0.
Derived Gibbs contrast numerator using Q_k/q_(k+1)=sum exp(beta_b(E_(k+1)-E_i)). Positive gaps give the same strict sign in every coordinate on either side of the bath.
On heating N,T>0; Nprime/N>-E_(k+1) and Tprime/T<=-E_(k+1). The quotient derivative is strictly positive.
Likelihood ratio has constant coefficient one and contrast coordinates g; reversibility evolves them by exp(tA). Its positive diagonal preserves strict positive coordinate differences.
Orthonormality equates weighted squared distance with squared coordinate norm, proving the strict all-time heating inequality for that distance.
Spectral expansion gives Pi2=lim exp(-lambda2 t)exp(tA), nonnegative and nonzero. A vector with all entries of the same strict sign cannot be annihilated, including degenerate slow eigenspaces.
Nonzero orthogonal projection has a positive diagonal entry. With g,gprime>0, this gives 2(Pi2 g) dot (Pi2 gprime)>0. The local KL expansion has the same leading squared norm.

For simple slow mode, maximizing the symmetric quadratic form over the sphere and replacing coordinates by absolute values gives a nonnegative top eigenvector. Its dot product with g gives the stated strict overlap signs and heating monotonicity.

Specialized the off-diagonal formula to the three printed aggregate inequalities for four states. The subsequent single-cooling-interval paragraph still depends on the separately unreviewed global stationary-point bound.
first_three_mode_restriction: B is positively diagonally similar to symmetric Metzler A; choose nonnegative top eigenvector x. Expanding Hx gives both easy inequalities and w1+w2-2w3=(2Q3/q3)(x2-sx1).
G puts a minimum reduced conductance in the first row. Subtracting k*(q 1transpose-Q4 I) leaves nonnegative reversible conservative rates with at least one of a12,a13,a14 zero.
Reset contributions cancel in F and G. Contrast B shifts by k*Q4 I, preserving eigenvectors, ordering and simple multiplicity. Dirichlet form gives shifted lambda<=0 even when reducible.
If x1=0 the desired inequality is immediate. Otherwise symmetric Rayleigh quotient gives lambda>=B33.

If equality held, positive semidefiniteness of lambda I-A forces its third row to vanish, by principal two-by-two minors. Then e3 is a top eigenvector; simplicity implies x1=0, contradiction. Thus delta=lambda-B33>0, including lambda=0.
Eliminating x3 gives Eij=Bij+Bi3 B3j/delta. Positive-pivot Schur complement preserves semidefiniteness and nullity one, so lambda is its simple top eigenvalue. Off-diagonals remain nonnegative.
For positive off-diagonals, r=x2/x1 is the unique positive zero of E21+r(E22-E11)-r^2 E12. Nonnegative value at s>0 implies s<=r.

If one off-diagonal vanishes, diagonal symmetrizability makes both vanish. Simple top eigenvalue and x1>0 force x2=0 and E11>E22, making the polynomial strictly negative at s>0. Nonnegativity excludes this boundary case.
Verified delta times the ratio polynomial equals delta C+D*. G gives B31,B32>=0; G134 and G234 bound the two negative terms in B23-s B13. Thus D*>=0.
For C>=0 the sign follows immediately. For C<0, lambda<=0 gives delta C+D*>=-B33 C+D*, with the correct inequality direction.
Verified the positive prefactor times T=(c+e+f)N+q4(2ceq3(q1-q2)+fJ), where N=-2q1q2q3 F123>=0.
Face c=0 gives J>=0. Face a=0 writes J as (2q1+q3)/(2q1+q4) times -2q1q2 F124 plus 2e q1(q1-q2)(q3-q4)/(2q1+q4). Both terms are nonnegative without dividing by c or e.
For b=0,c>e, N+q4J=2q1q2(q3-q4)(c-e)+d q1q3(2q2+q3)-2q1q2q3 F124>=0. Rewrite T=(c+e)N+f(N+q4J)+2ceq3q4(q1-q2).
The three zero-rate faces are exhaustive after reset and allow overlaps. No irreducibility of the shifted generator is assumed. This completes x2>=s x1, hence the stated first-three inequalities.
